To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the structure of a pseudo- 16-mer DNA complexed with the RT fragment reveals that (i) a pyrimidine nucleotide at the 3'-end of the DNA makes interactions with the strictly-conserved Gly191 and Leu115 that are indistinguishable from those made by a purine; (ii) the mispairs are located in a G-C rich region; and (iii) the three consecutive G's of the 10-nt strand induce a guanine stack and

the structure of a DNA molecule in a crystal lattice containing a protein molecule has been determined and that it has been shown that a pyrimidyl nucleotide in the 3'-OH position of a DNA molecule can make the same interactions with the protein molecule as a purinyl nucleotide.

a DNA molecule complex with MMLV RT has been crystallized and the structure determined to 2.0-A resolution, which is the first structure to be determined of any DNA molecule complex with a reverse transcriptase.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the structure of the N-terminal fragment (amino acids 1-115) of the MMLV RT bound to a 6/10-base-pair duplex containing two G-A mispair sites, which was crystallized in the space group P4(1)2(1)2, with unit-cell parameters a = b = 43.2, c = 91.8 A.
the structure of the complex of the N-terminal fragment (residues 1-113) of Moloney Murine Leukemia Virus (MMLV) reverse transcriptase with a pseudo-hexadecermer DNA.
the structure of the N-terminal fragment (amino acid residues 1-110) of MMLV reverse transcriptase (RT) in complex with a 16-base-pair DNA molecule containing a G-C-rich region.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the crystal structure is that of a pseudo-14-mer, with two additional G-A mispairs.
the structure of a DNA complexed with the MMLV RT N-terminal domain has been determined to 2 A resolution, and the structure is similar to that of the previous fragment-DNA complex.
the DNA in the present structure is a pseudo-hexadeca-mer with a G-C-rich sequence and a G-A mismatch, which is complexed to the N-terminal domain of MMLV reverse transcriptase.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the structure provides a detailed description of the interactions of the RT fragment with the DNA, which is consistent with the proposed mechanistical role of the RT fragment in DNA synthesis by RT.
this structure represents the first example of a DNA fragment in complex with a protein that is not a primer-template.
the structure of the MMLV fragment-DNA complex shows that the DNA is not distorted by the binding of the fragment.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the crystallographic environment can have a profound effect on DNA structure and that the crystal structure of a DNA fragment complexed with a protein can provide a unique and valuable structural model for that DNA in the absence of the protein.

, although the DNA in this structure is not a substrate for MMLV RT, the interactions with the protein are very similar to those observed in a previous structure of MMLV fragment-DNA complex, which was a good substrate for the enzyme.
a DNA structure can be determined in a protein-DNA crystal lattice without bias from the protein, provided that the DNA is designed to be a suitable substrate for the protein.
